risk-rmf-functions.hint: Drag each activity onto its function. Govern runs across all of them; Map establishes context, Measure quantifies, Manage acts.
risk-rmf-functions.note: Govern is not a phase that finishes. If an activity sets the conditions under which the other three happen — culture, accountability, policy — it is Govern, whenever it occurs.
risk-rmf-functions.zones[0].def: Cultivate a culture of risk management: policies, accountability structures, roles, workforce capability, third-party oversight. Cuts across the other three.
risk-rmf-functions.zones[1].def: Establish context and frame risks: purpose, setting, actors, impacted people, capabilities and limitations, interdependencies.
risk-rmf-functions.zones[2].def: Analyse, assess, benchmark and monitor using quantitative and qualitative methods, including the trustworthiness characteristics.
risk-rmf-functions.zones[3].def: Allocate resources to mapped and measured risks: prioritise, respond, recover, communicate, and act on third-party and residual risk.

rmf-01.label: The organisation documents who is accountable for AI risk decisions and at what level each class of decision may be taken.
rmf-01.why: Accountability structures are the archetypal GOVERN activity. Without them the other three functions have no one to report to and no one to escalate to.

rmf-02.label: An AI policy is approved, aligned to legal requirements, and its exceptions process is defined.
rmf-02.why: Policy and its exception route set the conditions under which every other activity happens. GOVERN is cross-cutting, not sequential.

rmf-03.label: Staff working on AI systems are given role-specific training and their competence is tracked.
rmf-03.why: Workforce capability sits squarely in GOVERN. A measurement regime nobody is competent to run produces numbers without assurance.

rmf-04.label: Processes are established for overseeing third-party models and data, including what must be obtained from suppliers.
rmf-04.why: GOVERN explicitly covers third-party oversight policy. Applying it to a specific vendor's risk on a specific system is MANAGE.

rmf-05.label: The team documents the system's intended purpose, deployment setting, and the categories of people it will affect.
rmf-05.why: Framing context is the whole point of MAP. Skipping it is how a system is later measured accurately against the wrong objective.

rmf-06.label: Known capabilities, limitations and assumptions of the system are catalogued, including where it should not be used.
rmf-06.why: MAP establishes what the system is and is not for. The out-of-scope statement authored here is what later evaluation and monitoring are judged against.

rmf-07.label: Internal and external stakeholders, including affected communities, are identified along with the benefits and potential harms to each.
rmf-07.why: Identifying impacted parties and framing potential impacts is MAP. Quantifying those impacts is MEASURE.

rmf-08.label: Interdependencies with other systems and the consequences of the AI component failing are traced.
rmf-08.why: MAP covers the system in its wider context, including what else breaks when it does. A component viewed in isolation is a mapped risk missed.

rmf-09.label: The system is benchmarked against defined metrics for validity, reliability and robustness before release.
rmf-09.why: MEASURE covers assessment against the trustworthiness characteristics using repeatable methods.

rmf-10.label: Performance is evaluated separately for each demographic subgroup and the disparity is quantified.
rmf-10.why: Analysing harmful bias with quantitative methods is MEASURE. Deciding what to do about the disparity is MANAGE.

rmf-11.label: Ongoing monitoring instruments the deployed system for input drift and quality degradation.
rmf-11.why: MEASURE includes continuous monitoring after deployment, not only pre-release testing. Drift detection lives here.

rmf-12.label: Test, evaluation, verification and validation methods are chosen, documented, and their own limitations recorded.
rmf-12.why: MEASURE requires that the measurement approach itself be assessed. A metric with unexamined blind spots is a false assurance.

rmf-13.label: Risks are prioritised against impact and resources are allocated to the highest first.
rmf-13.why: Prioritisation and resource allocation across mapped and measured risks is the definition of MANAGE.

rmf-14.label: A response plan is put in place covering incident containment, recovery and communication for a model failure.
rmf-14.why: MANAGE covers responding to, recovering from and communicating about incidents. Writing the plan is MANAGE; rehearsing capability is GOVERN.

rmf-15.label: Residual risk after mitigation is documented and communicated to the deployer of the system.
rmf-15.why: MANAGE explicitly addresses residual risk, including telling downstream users what remains. Undocumented residual risk is transferred by accident.

rmf-16.label: A decision is taken to decommission a deployed model whose risk can no longer be brought within tolerance.
rmf-16.why: Superseding or decommissioning a system is a MANAGE response. Having a defined route to retirement is what makes it possible.
